title: The world according to the Hereford Mappa Mundi
excerpt: I set the largest surviving medieval map of the world beside a modern one. Its directions from Jerusalem are mostly right; its scale is not: the Holy Land is drawn 4.5 times too big, and Britain has 8% of its names.
seo_description: The Hereford Mappa Mundi (c. 1300) beside a modern map: 1,025 names, where it puts real places, and what is Biblical, classical or legend.
header_alt: Title card reading 'Mappa Mundi' in black and red on pale parchment, beside Konrad Miller's facsimile of the Hereford map dotted with coloured markers, and a small modern map of Europe, Africa and Asia with the same places. Text: 1,025 names, Jerusalem at the centre, east at the top.
